text: A method extracted purely to give a section of code a name, with only one caller, is over-engineering.
explanation: Naming is the point, and reuse is a frequent side effect rather than the justification. A method called once, whose name says what a dozen lines do, has replaced a comment with something the compiler checks and a stack trace can mention. Chapter 11 puts it directly: naming is not labelling something you already built, it is how you decide what to build.
